topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the scope of the cancer lecture course, and the primary learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer mechanisms.

topics.label: Origins, Drivers, and Epidemiological Evidence of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the core nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease influenced by a balance of intrinsic biological errors, genetic predispositions, and environmentally driven exposures demonstrated through epidemiological data.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Pathogen, Chemical, and Physical Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific biological agents, dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical exposures induce DNA damage, adduct formation, and oncogenic cellular alterations.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation, Promotion, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanistic distinction between cancer initiators and inflammatory or proliferative promoters, as well as the influence of host developmental timing and tissue context on malignant transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical tools, mutational signature profiling, epidemiological approaches, and experimental model systems used to detect and prove the carcinogenic effects of compounds.

topics.label: Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure within practical risk-benefit decision-making and summarizing the primary challenges in determining carcinogenic potency.
